data.name: github
data.description: Use the GitHub REST API as yourself, through your own GitHub account. With it you can create repos, write and update files, publish GitHub Pages sites, open and answer issues, read what people say about your work, check your stats, and do anything else the API allows. Give an HTTP method, a path such as /user/repos, and an optional JSON body. To create or update a file: PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path} with body {"message": "...", "content_text": "<the file's text>"}. content_text is base64-encoded for you; when updating an existing file, include its current "sha". Noisy *_url fields are trimmed from responses unless raw is true. (GitHub has no API for changing your profile picture; ask your human for that.)

data.name: http
data.description: Make any HTTP request on the web: call APIs, submit forms, download things. Give a method, a url, optional headers, and a body (json for a JSON body, form for a form-encoded body, or body for raw text). Anywhere in the headers, url or body you can write {{CHARLIE_SOMETHING}} (or {{GITHUB_TOKEN}}), and it is replaced with that secret from your environment, so you never have to see or type it. Returns the status, the important headers, and the response body: JSON is parsed, and HTML is reduced to readable text unless raw is true. Use web_fetch to just read a page; use this to act.

data.name: bluesky
data.description: Use Bluesky as yourself (your own account). Actions: "post" (text up to 300 characters; links in the text become clickable, and link adds a preview card for a URL); "reply" (to a post: uri, plus text); "notifications" (likes, replies, follows, mentions); "my_posts" (with likes, reposts and replies); "profile" (yours, or anyone's with actor); "update_profile" (any of display_name, bio, avatar and banner, where avatar and banner are PNG or JPEG files in your home folder up to 1 MB; avatars show as a circle, banners are 3:1); "search" (posts: query); "thread" (a post and its replies: uri).

data.name: devvit
data.description: Get onto Reddit through Reddit's own developer platform (Devvit), as your Reddit account. Reddit's regular API is closed to you, so this is your way in: apps and games that live inside Reddit posts, built with web tech (templates: react, phaser, threejs, bare). Actions: "setup" (the first time: creates your app from the code your human gave you; optional template), "status", "files" (list your app's files), "read" (path), "write" (files: { path: content } to create or overwrite files in your app), "upload" (build and upload a new version; it's installed to your own test subreddit automatically), "install" (subreddit you moderate), "publish" (submit for Reddit's review; public: true to list it publicly), "logs" (subreddit, since such as "1h"; your app's recent logs), "run" (args: any other devvit command, e.g. ["settings","list"]). Devvit docs: https://developers.reddit.com/docs

data.name: edit_file
data.description: Find-and-replace edits on a text file inside my home folder (e.g. site/photobooth/index.html), or copy a home file into a path. Use before publish_page with from_file, so small page fixes don't need full republishing. Also can report size/grep lines. NEW: push_to_repo {repo:"owner/name", path:"dir/file.html", message} uploads the (edited) file to GitHub (creates or updates), so site files can be mirrored to repos without pasting.
